_readme:
Hand-set level overrides, applied after the frequency ranking and the CEFR-J anchor.

  pin     — force to level 1 (A1). Almost all conversational: greetings, politeness, yes/no. The ranking sources structurally under-rate them (an encyclopedia never says hello, and `por favor` / `s'il vous plaît` are not single tokens at all), so `hola` and `bonjour` came out at B1.
  demote  — force no higher than DEMOTE_FLOOR (B1). The mirror problem: French ranks off Lexique, whose two registers are film subtitles and books, BOTH narrative fiction, so death and war vocabulary is genuinely frequent and lands in A1. Frequency is not wrong about these words; they are simply not what a beginner should meet first.

Blending in news/Wikipedia was measured and makes it WORSE, not better: those registers rank `guerre` 206/72 and `mort` 144/78 while burying `bonjour` at 4348/16922 and `merci` at 11506. Conflict vocabulary is core news and encyclopedia vocabulary. No weighting of that signal separates the two, so this list is an editorial judgement, stated plainly, rather than a number pretending to be one.

Spanish `demote` holds two kinds of leak. Bound fragments — `a través de`, `a menudo`, `sin embargo`, `acerca de`, `llevar a cabo` — where the corpus frequency belongs to the phrase but the gloss is a rare standalone sense (`través` is banded on "a través de" and glossed "bend, turn"). And proper nouns the name filter could not catch: their corpus frequency is the country's or the name's (text is lowercased before counting) while the surviving gloss is a rare common noun — `brasil` is banded on the country but glossed "brazilwood", `maría` on the given name but glossed "magpie".

Keep both lists short. Every entry must be a real dictionary headword; the build warns and skips anything that is not. A word in both lists is a config error and `pin` wins. See scripts/lib/coreOverrides.mjs.
